o1.biggest_strength: Hooks are lifted straight from real customer comments and the data logic (test and swap in front, label in the middle, founder dropped) is stated openly so I trust the choices.
o1.biggest_mistake: Disclosure is buried in the standing rules rather than written into each script or brief, so a creator could miss it, and the price handling on Script 1 is left thin.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put the Meta Paid Partnership label and TikTok branded-content toggle explicitly inside each creator brief and on-screen in the first seconds of every script, and give each script a one-line price answer.

o2.biggest_strength: Looks genuinely shoot-ready: a summary table up front, disclosure written into every script and into the shared brief, exact-word lines marked, plus deliverables, rights and timing spelled out.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 'Exact' lines are a bit stiff and read less like a real creator's words, and the board of banned words is strong but the creators get a little less conversational freedom than the brief promised.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Loosen the locked lines so they sound like a person talking, and add one alternate hook per script that is a straight customer comment rather than a written line.

reason: Both get the data right and stay on brand, but Option 2 is the one I could actually send to creators today: disclosure is built into every script and brief, and it lists deliverables, rights and timing. Option 1 is strong but leaves me to add those pieces myself.
